=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- scripts/drift_audit.sh:lines ≈ 604-507 in the function body | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
  Problem: The helper strips all diff-line prefixes (via `line_prefixes` parameter that is never used for `+`/`-` discrimination) before applying the regex. The same function is called for both `must_contain` and `must_not_contain` fingerprints.
  Why it fails at runtime: When a PR removes a line that previously matched a `must_contain` fingerprint, `_cluster_resolved_by_pr_files` can incorrectly return `true` for that fingerprint, causing the drift-audit job to close the tracker issue even though the required content is gone. This defeats the whole point of the “persistent drift” tracker.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh:lines ≈ 517 | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
  Problem: The function treats a removed file (status == "removed") as a resolution for *any* fingerprint kind, including `must_contain`.
  Why it fails at runtime: Deleting the file that was supposed to contain a required pattern is counted as “the violation has been fixed”, so tracker issues for must-contain drift can be closed when the root cause is still present on integration.
- scripts/drift_audit.sh:≈ line 1450 | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  Problem: The dynamically generated query only creates `i0:`, `i1:`, … aliases up to the batch size, but the result-processing code assumes node `iN` always exists for every supplied issue number. If the batch size is truncated or an issue number is missing from the response, the recheck for that issue is silently dropped.
  Why it fails at runtime: Issues that carry persistent `PRE_EXISTING_FINGERPRINT_DRIFT_V1` markers can be omitted from the daily drift-audit re-evaluation, allowing long-lived false-positive trackers to remain open forever.
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
